title: Annotatio V §.IV: Author’s three charges — doubt Institution; deny presence; erase sacramental vs spiritual
pass_a_gloss: And so the Author, about first to enervate my points by which I had held that Negation of the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body — both absolute and related to the unworthy — does not wound the foundation of faith, even if it be granted to wander from the true and the opposite affirmation to be nearer the Holy Spirit’s mind, says (1) It is no matter of slight moment to call into doubt a Doctrine clearly and perspicuously set forth in Scripture and to detract faith from Christ’s words pronouncing of the whole complex: Eat, drink, this is my Body. (2) That he who denies the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body also denies its true and Substantial presence in the Supper. (3) That the same denies Sacramental Eating and leaves no remaining distinction between Spiritual and Sacramental Eating §. XI.
pass_b_english: The Author first tries to break Strimesius’s claim that denying Oral (absolute or as to the unworthy) does not wound faith’s foundation — even if Oral were nearer the Spirit’s mind.

Three charges (§. XI): (1) to doubt Oral is to doubt clear Institution words and make Christ a liar; (2) denying Oral denies true substantial presence; (3) it denies sacramental eating and erases spiritual/sacramental distinction.
source_text: Itaque mea prius enervaturus Autor, quibus perhibueram, Negationem Oralis Manducationis Corporis Christi, tam absolutam, quàm ad indignos relatam, haud lædere fundamentum fidei, etiamsi à verô aberrare, & affirmatio opposita, Spiritûs S. menti vicinior esse, concedatur; dicit (1) Non exigui momenti rem esse, Doctrinam in Scriptura clare & perspicuè propositam, vocare in dubium & fidem verbis Christi detrahere, de toto sympeplegmenô pronunciantis: Edite, bibite, hoc est Corpus meum. (2) Eum qui negat Oralem Corporis Christi Manducationem, etiam negare veram & Substantialem præsentiam ejusdem in Cœna. (3) Eundem negare Manducationem Sacramentalem, nec ullum inter Manducationem Spiritualem & Sacramentalem discrimen reliquum facere §. XI.

lemmas.gloss: to detract faith from Christ’s words
